notes: Found the crash, and it was only ever possible in the installed app. Every version SideCut has ever run stores a copy of its own page (about 1.8 MB) so you can roll back to it, and none of those are ever removed. The app also mirrors a small recovery file to the device so your playlists, albums and settings survive a reinstall — and that mirror was carrying up to FIFTY of those page copies with it. Because the file is rewritten shortly after any change, and playing a song changes the playback position every few seconds, the app was building a 30-90 MB piece of text on the main thread and writing it to the disk every few seconds while you listened. That is a memory spike big enough for Android to kill the app outright (the random crash after playing a song), a stalled main thread (songs stuttering or stopping), and constant writes to flash (why the battery drained so fast). It is behind a native-only check, which is exactly why the browser version never showed any of it

The mirror now carries what it is for — playlists, albums, settings — and no page copies at all. Measured on the same library: the app used to write 8.6 MB per write with only twelve versions of history (yours has far more), and now writes about 0.6 KB

The recovery file has a hard 1 MB ceiling. If something oversized ever tries to get in, the biggest entry is dropped and reported instead of writing a huge file, and if it still would not fit the write is skipped rather than blocking the app
It also stops writing when nothing changed, and while the app is in the background it writes at most once every ten seconds instead of whenever anything moves
